result.title: CommunityKV: Efficient Long-Context Decoding via Graph Partitioning
result.summary: Scaling Transformers to long contexts is constrained by the quadratic cost of self-attention and the linear growth of key-value cache memory transfer. Sparse attention mitigates this by retrieving only relevant tokens, but current approaches either require large-scale training or, within the training-free regime, rely on semantically coarse heuristics or expensive clustering that is difficult to update efficiently during decoding. We introduce CommunityKV, a framework that formulates sparse attention as a community detection problem. CommunityKV constructs a token graph from the $QK^T$ scores already computed during standard prefill, and partitions the graph into communities to enable retrieval of semantically coherent token groups. A local update rule assigns newly generated tokens to communities in constant time, enabling sparse retrieval throughout streaming decoding without global re-partitioning. We evaluate CommunityKV on Qwen3 and Llama-3.1 models across three long-context benchmarks. With one graph per query head, CommunityKV delivers up to $1.25\times$ the end-to-end generation throughput of dense attention, while query-group graph aggregation yields up to $1.71\times$ with comparable accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: CommunityKV 把稀疏注意力重构为社区发现问题：在预填充阶段已有的 QK^T 分数上构建 token 图并划分社区，再用常数时间的局部更新规则把新生成 token 归入社区，从而在长上下文流式解码中免训练地检索语义连贯的 token 组。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线不直接相关（属训练无关的长上下文解码效率优化），但其按语义相关性组织 token 单元、并支持增量局部更新的做法，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、KV/状态缓存更新与获取成本权衡提供可核查的方法线索。
